feature: Lift keeps both halves as the same clip
summary: Lifting a marked stretch out of a clip now leaves both halves called what the clip is called, the way Command K and Extract do. Before, the half after the gap came back as Sample Talk copy.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any screen recording with sound and open the timeline. The walk lift-keeps-one-clip-walk does all of this on its own sample talk.

try.do: Move the playhead to about 0:04 and press I, then to about 0:08 and press O.
Press semicolon: the stretch goes, the gap stays, and both halves on V1 carry the clip's name.
Press Command Z: the clip is whole again.
Right-click the clip on V1, choose Detach Audio, then mark the same stretch and press semicolon again.
Look at Audio: both halves of the sound keep the sound's name, and both halves on V1 keep the clip's name.
Pick the middle piece of a clip you cut twice with Command K and press Delete: both sides keep the clip name.

evaluate: Does a lifted clip now read as one clip with a hole in it rather than as two different clips?
With two halves showing the same name, can you still tell which one you have picked?
Would you expect the half after the gap to carry a number (Sample Talk · 2), as the cut mock draws it?
rough: The cut walkthrough mock labels the part after a blade cut screen-recording · 2; the app shows the plain clip name on both parts, for Command K and now Lift. Open as decision card the-part-after-a-cut-is-labelled-the-way-the-cut-after-you-cut-a-clip-or-lift-a-s on task the-part-after-a-cut-is-labelled-the-way-the-cut.
A lifted clip is two clips that share a name, not one clip in two pieces: a clip's pieces sit back to back and cannot hold a gap. Premiere's Lift leaves the same two clip items.
The canvas is black straight after the lift because the playhead sits at the In, which is now the start of the gap.
